{"description":"RE-SCOPED (2026-08-25): JSON vectors are NOT the right artifact for key persistence; coverage is behavioral-only by design.

Evidence:
- lichen.crypto.key_persistence (FileKeyStore/TrustStorePersistence) is filesystem-behavioral: two-slot crash-safe writes, flock inter-process locks, O_NOFOLLOW/0600 permission enforcement, SHA-256-anchored rollback detection, HMAC-authenticated trust-store documents. These are OS-interaction properties, not pure functions over wire bytes, so language-neutral JSON vectors cannot exercise them.
- The only serializable wire surface (KEY1 slot header format) is implemented ONLY by the Python reference: no KEY1 magic exists anywhere in rust/lichen-core, rust/lichen-link, c/, or lichen/subsys (repo-wide grep verified 2026-08-25). JSON vectors for it would have exactly one consumer - a self-oracle, violating test-integrity discipline.
- test/vectors/keystore_cbor.json already covers the /keys CoAP resource CBOR representation (spec 17.5.5), consumed by python/tests/crypto/test_keystore_vectors.py - different topic from seed persistence.

Real coverage (run green 2026-08-25):
  cd python && uv run --extra dev pytest tests/crypto/test_key_persistence.py -q
  => 63 passed (MemoryKeyStore, FileKeyStore two-slot/crash/anchor/conflict paths, TrustStorePersistence tamper/tamper-check/limits)
Sibling l1qw.6.11.1.4 "Validate: Cross-check ... oracle" says "Run oracle against existing vectors if any" - there are none by this decision; validate against the behavioral suite above instead.
","title":"Key Persistence: behavioral-only coverage (re-scoped from JSON vectors)"}

Re-scoped: key persistence is behavioral-only (filesystem/locks/anchors, no second KEY1-format implementation exists for cross-consumption). Real coverage = python/tests/crypto/test_key_persistence.py (63 passed 2026-08-25); keystore_cbor.json covers the separate /keys CBOR topic. No vectors faked.
